dedupe_keys.name: faa national wildlife strike database nwsd

description: The National Wildlife Strike Database holds reports of collisions between wildlife and civil aircraft in the United States and US-registered aircraft abroad, kept by the Federal Aviation Administration's Office of Airports Safety and Standards. The FAA's annual report for 1990 to 2025 counts 343,556 strikes reported over 36 years, 98.3 percent of them in the United States, from 2,417 airports; 24,447 were reported in 2025 at 870 airports (454 Part 139 certificated and 416 general aviation). Reports come mostly through the electronic FAA Form 5200-7, and some through the Air Traffic Organization's mandatory occurrence reporting, with species identified by the Smithsonian Feather Identification Laboratory; reports record the airport, time of occurrence, phase of flight, height above ground, species, components struck and damaged, and effect on flight. The database can be searched and the data explored free online, and the annual report adds tables by airport type, height, damage and species. Caveats: reporting is voluntary for most operators, so the absolute number of strikes is unknown and rising counts partly reflect better reporting; the FAA therefore tracks rates of damaging strikes per 100,000 movements. The data support hazard exposure and resilience analyses of airport operations and complement the FAA ASIAS safety data.
